sections.h: Note on the text. Translated from the Italian original. The signs [?] mark passages that are uncertain or damaged in the original.

This collection brings together, in order of date, everything that is preserved in the archive “03 · CARISMA FSA” of the circular letters of Mother Rosa to the Daughters of Saint Anne, from 1875 to 1895. The circulars up to 1887 are signed jointly with Fr. Giovanni Battista Tornatore.

Three kinds of text, indicated beneath each title:

  • Full text — eight circulars (1888-1894) transcribed from a printed booklet of the Circulars.
  • Excerpt — passages reproduced in the anthology “Attingiamo alle Fonti”, with the archive position (IIC, B.1.63-64) of the Generalate of the Daughters of Saint Anne; the dots and the parentheses (…) are the anthology’s.
  • Portuguese translation — by Fr. Valdo; for the circular of 20 August 1895 it is the only complete text available.

The complete originals of all the circulars are in the archive of the Generalate (positions IIC 75-95). Dates without a day are those given by the source.

[Excerpt]

…At present the Institute numbers twenty-three houses and three hundred sisters; in the year just ended, 1874, six houses were founded, and in the year 1875, scarcely begun, there are already requests.

To whom, sisters, do we owe so rapid an expansion of the Institute, in the few years since it was born? Certainly to the mercy of the Heavenly Father, who has been pleased to bless it. In general the sisters are animated by the Spirit of their own vocation; they keep before their eyes the end for which the Lord has raised them to the great nobility of being daughters of Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate, which end is to consecrate their whole life to blessing Him, and thanking Him, and praising Him for all the wonders wrought in their Holy Mother, and for the greatest of them all, that is, of having made her Mother of the Immaculate, His Mother Mary Most Holy, and to imitate her in all her virtues, which are taught us by our Holy Rules.

Above all, three points serve to attain the aforesaid end: first, punctuality at rising, so that as soon as they hear the five o’clock bell, at once, and without letting even a moment pass, they get up; second, that at half past five they be all already in the Chapel to begin the meditation…

Source: Circolare 1875 · Posiz. Archivio: IIC 75 B.1.63

[Excerpt]

Behold, sisters, the year just ended too was full of heavenly blessings for our poor Institute.

May the Heavenly Father, who is the one who planted it in the garden of His Church, look upon it with an eye of special predilection: He increased its houses and multiplied its members.

Of new houses, in the past year there have been opened (9), and of sisters there have been clothed (46); with the expansion of the Houses and with the increase of the sisters He has been pleased to strengthen it ever better in the spirit of its vocation.

The Lord raised up our Institute so that it might be the family of the glorious Saint Anne, August Mother of Mary Immaculate; in which family the great Saint might be honoured, loved and imitated. And in general the sisters respond to this purpose. They imitate the life which their Mother, while living on this earth, led for the benefit of her neighbour.

The service which they give to the sick, both in the hospitals and in their homes, is done with a spirit of faith and with a love of sacrifice which clearly show that they keep in mind the divine words of Jesus Christ, who assures us that the care given to the sick for love of Him He reckons as done to Himself. No less vigilant is the care of those who are employed in teaching school: to imitate the piety of our Holy Mother. They spend on it all the talent they have received from the Lord, so that their pupils may be good before God and before men; they bring them up dear to Jesus Christ, and such as to be afterwards the consolation of their families. The [?] sign of this spirit of their vocation which animates them is that, by divine goodness, they win in general the sympathy of those cities and towns where they work. Of this sympathy our Bishops, in whose Dioceses we have houses, have given open testimony. They have drawn up the most cordial and expressive letters of commendation, in which letters the sisters are greatly praised, and their zeal, and their wise and modest conduct, by which they are an edification to their people (…) Not only do the Bishops speak well of us, but we are also respected and honoured by the Secular authorities. But what crowns our joy is the love which the Vicar of Jesus Christ bears to our poor Institute (…)

Behold, sisters, the loveliness of our Holy Mother, which drew to her the affection of the heart of God, of the divine heart of Jesus and of Mary: she pours it out upon us, and makes us objects of affection to heaven and to all the noblest creatures the earth has; but the signs of affection of the Heavenly Father and of the Holy Mother would not have been complete if, with the consolations that accompanied our family in the year just ended, tribulations had not been mingled.

Yes, the crosses, which are the mark of the chosen works of God, were not lacking to us; two especially were keenly felt by us, and these were the taking from us of its sisters most zealous and laborious in expanding the Institute and increasing its glory: you already understand me, that we mourn the loss of Sister Anna Vincenza and of Sister Anna Francesca; yes, we can bear witness that the love they had for increasing the splendour of their Holy Mother was what made them two victims and sacrificed them for the good of her family; but the Lord has so willed: may His adorable will always be done.

In so great a loss, however, we have reason to console ourselves, and this reason is that the example they have left us will be a spur to us to imitate them, and not to be content until we reach the point of being able to say: the love we have had for our God, for the glory of the Holy Mother and for the expansion of her Institute has taken our life. What is the gratitude God asks of us for the favours with which He has filled us in the year now ended? He wants a deep sentiment of humility by which we confess that we have not merited them… and may it make us confess before His Divine Majesty that we are His unprofitable Servants…

The second thing He wants of us is that we be attentive to the Observance of the Rules… in particular punctuality at rising… rising is the first sacrifice He asks of us in the day: if this sacrifice is made with the promptness He requires, then it merits for us a special grace to make the Holy meditation well, and on a meditation well made depends our spiritual progress (…)

If the institute holds firm to these cardinal points of the rule, then it will be a solid edifice that will not fear the assaults in [?] its enemies, be they of the world or the demons of hell; it will be an object of joy to the Holy Mother, where she will be glorified, loved and imitated by her daughters; and they will then merit, at the end of their days, the crown of glory which the Lord holds prepared for those who serve Him with a true heart.

Source: Lettera circolare 1876 · Posiz. Archivio: IIC 76 B.1.63

[Excerpt]

… wherever we are they love us and are glad to see us, and so it is too with the faithful, who appreciate our duties, and very many are the sick of every condition who ask for our assistance, both in their homes and in the hospitals…

… it may be said that the sisters, in general, love the Lord with all their heart. But not all have been faithful in the year just ended… We shall mention some faults into which they have fallen. One of the faults… was the poor bearing of the Daughters of Saint Anne in the street. It must be at once natural and modest…

Behold, sisters, the reason for grief and weeping that some of you have… This amendment the Lord asks, in gratitude for having waited for us in mercy until this new year; the Holy Mother asks it, who keeps us in her Family; our neighbours ask it, who can hope for nothing good from relaxed sisters, but will rather be badly edified by them…

Source: Lettere · Posiz. Archivio: IIC 77-1 B.1.63 · Lettere · Posiz. Archivio: B.1.63 [?] IIC 86

[Excerpt]

Oh! how good is the God of Israel! So we have every reason to exclaim, seeing the great mercies with which He has filled us this year too.

Yes, His most merciful eyes were continually open upon our poor Institute. The Daughter of Saint Anne no longer lives for herself, but lives for her Institute; therefore she takes account of its benefits, those which the Lord poured out upon the Family of the Holy Mother.

The principal benefit, which must be counted before all others, is that of having granted to the sisters, in general, the grace of observance.

Among the virtues I shall touch only on holy indifference, which is as it were the uniform of the Daughters of Saint Anne, which keeps them detached from everything so as to be ready for any place whatever where obedience may wish to send them: yes, with the greatest joy of our heart we must say that in general none ever put forward excuses for not moving from the house where she was living to go to the one to which we assigned her. So too the ready spirit with which they devoted themselves to the care of the sick and to the education of young girls was to be admired… (…) The relations, moreover, which our Institute maintains with those outside are consoling in every respect.

And first of all, how the Holy Father continues in his predilection towards us!!! Among the many proofs he has given of this special affection of his, an outstanding one is that which we received most recently, namely that he deigned to buy us a fine house and [?] Rome at the place called the Parrocchietta, where a School of ours flourishes…

What calls we have had to open new houses, so much so that this year eleven [?] houses have been opened. The numerous vocations attest to us the esteem of the people in general; indeed this year [? (&) ?] sisters have been clothed.

This esteem which we enjoy among people of the world we must value only as a sign that our Institute is of spiritual and temporal advantage to the Church. And hence that the Lord is glorified through us, as we correspond to the proximate end for which He has placed us in His Church, which is that of honouring, and making all honour, the August and glorious Mother of the Immaculate, our Mother Saint Anne; and at the same time it must make us reflect how the protection of the Holy Mother over us and those [?] which draw upon us from heaven all these blessings, and it must enkindle us ever more with holy and fervent and filial affection towards this most high and most tender Mother of ours, for she is for us that channel through which, from heaven, by the hands of Mary her Immaculate Daughter, all graces come to us…

Source: Circolare 1878 di M. Rosa e P.G.B. Tornatore · Posiz. Archivio: IIC 78.1 B.1.63

[Excerpt]

The year now ending, 1878, sets before our eyes, O dearest sisters and daughters, the benefits we have received from the Lord in its course. Oh! how numerous and great they are! One, and the most signal, is the benevolence with which the Vicar, the Supreme Pontiff happily reigning, Leo XIII, regards our Institute. He has not only confirmed to us the donation of the House and vineyard of the Parrocchietta, which the late Holy Father of holy memory made to us towards the end of his days, but at his own expense he had the said house restored. We know that he greatly rejoices to see how rapidly our Institute is spreading. This solicitude which the Vicar of Jesus Christ takes for the growth of our institute is an assurance to us that God finds His good pleasure in it. The Bishops too of the various Dioceses in which we have houses show themselves very satisfied with the duties we carry out there. We also win the sympathy of the people among whom we work. A proof of this sympathy we had from the people of Maratea, who, on the occasion of the high-handedness of a government Commissioner who wished to send away our teachers, opposed him all in a body and with all the power that was in their hands. But to what, dearest sisters and daughters, must we attribute so many blessings of heaven? To the prayers which our Holy Mother continually offers at the Throne of the Lord. It is to her prayers that we must ascribe the rapid expansion of the Institute: in this year now closing we have opened eleven houses, among which special mention is merited by the one we have founded in the new world, I mean in South America, where sixteen of our sisters have gone for the care of two hospitals in the city of La Paz. Ninety are the sisters who have been clothed this year. Behold, then, dearest sisters and daughters, how many and great are the benefits that call for our gratitude towards the Lord who has deigned to bestow them on us.

But in general we have reason to rejoice that in the houses of our Institute, in gratitude to God for so many and such great benefits received from Him, the fragrant sacrifice of the observance of the Holy Rules is offered; we are, however, compelled to deplore the non-observances of some sisters. And in the first place the spirit of those superiors is deplorable who show little affection for the Mother, who is as it were the centre and the heart of the institute. These unfortunate Superiors do not reflect that, as the ray detached from the centre is extinguished and the member detached from the heart dies, so they are dead members (…) The Mother House is as it were the heart of the Institute; therefore, as the members of the body are all solicitude that the heart may be robust, since life depends on it, so all good superiors are concerned that the Mother House be helped and be able to receive many postulants (…) While, then, on the one hand we are grateful to those good Superiors who show themselves true daughters of the Holy Mother and zealous that her family may grow, we exhort those of little zeal and love to imitate their example. (….)

To the sisters in general we recommend first diligence in being punctual at the works of piety, meditation, Mass, Communion, thanksgiving, prayers, chaplet, examen, Holy Rosary; punctuality at common acts, punctuality at rising, breakfast, dinner, supper and recreation. In the second place we recommend them to be industrious, carrying out well the duties entrusted to them. In the third place we recommend them to see in their superiors the person of Jesus Christ, and therefore to love them, respect them and obey them (…) Here, most beloved sisters and daughters, is what the Lord wants of us in order to show ourselves grateful for the benefits God has bestowed on us in the year just ended, and to be disposed to receive new ones, so as to have the consolation of seeing our Company flourish to the glory of God and of the Holy Mother…

Source: Circolare 1879 M. Rosa e P.G.B. Tornatore · Posiz. Archivio: IIC 79 B.1.63

[Excerpt]

Note: the text largely coincides with that of 31 January 1880; it is probably the same circular handed down through two archival sources (IIC 80-1 and IIC 80).

… Negotiations are under way to found there, likewise in America, three more Houses in three different cities, to which 40 Sisters would be called. This eagerness to have our sisters arises from seeing the prosperous results which the peoples who have them derive from them, both in the hospitals and in the schools. One of these goods which the Lord, by the hands of our sisters, is pleased to bestow [?] on His creatures, and which merits special mention, is the distribution of soup to the poor. In this winter of seventy-nine and eighty the Lord is chastising the sins of the world with cold and hunger. Well then, His mercy, which is never separated from His divine justice, has called us, His ministers, to succour so many wretched people, distributing to them every day food and clothing. In the Mother House alone about three thousand beggars are fed with good and well-seasoned soup. What a great grace this is, O Sisters! What a sign of predilection the Lord shows us! The way to thank Him for so great a distinction is to humble ourselves before His divine Majesty, sincerely acknowledging ourselves unworthy, and to work without sparing ourselves in carrying out so noble an office. The number of those clothed was 57, a number lower than that of ’78, but the cause was not the scarcity of postulants… but that, owing to the critical times we are living in, they have not been able to bring the dowry that is required, little though it is. On the other [?], the Mother House, because of the straitened times, has not been able to open its arms to receive them even without a dowry. And here comes the point of recommending economy especially to the Superiors, so that, after having maintained and clothed the sisters, they may send the surplus to the mother house. To this they are bound by love, by vow and by justice. By love: I must [?] know that the fruitfulness of the Institute depends on two heads; the first is that the Lord call many to it even with a very small dowry or none at all. Now the first head has not been lacking this year, for very many were the applications, but the Mother House has lacked the means to receive them without a dowry. Now on whom does it depend that the Mother House have these means? It depends precisely on the economy practised by the Superiors.

It is consoling to say that many true daughters of the Holy Mother, eager to see her family spread throughout the whole world, are most attentive to account even for the last penny, as the saying goes, so as to have a surplus to send to the Mother House, knowing that from the well-being of this arises the well-being of the whole Institute. The Mother House is the heart of the Institute. If the heart is full of life, the members of the other Houses too are healthy and robust. But this joy the Holy Mother does not receive from all. There are some of those spendthrifts who, notwithstanding handsome payments, never have anything to save. These are without love and unnatural, caring nothing for the glory of the Institute. These, besides being without love towards the Institute, put themselves in danger of failing in justice by damaging it… let them remember that they are not owners of the goods of the Houses over which they preside, but simple administrators. And it is a thing worth observing that, just as Superiors who love the Institute and are careful not to squander its goods also treat their sisters well, love them when healthy and care for them when sick, so those who live only for themselves and do not know how to save neglect the sisters and make them suffer…

Source: Lettere · Posiz. Archivio: IIC 80-1 B.1.63

[Excerpt]

Note: the text largely coincides with that of 1 January 1880; it is probably the same circular handed down through two archival sources (IIC 80-1 and IIC 80).

Behold, our Institute, the family of the August and Glorious Saint Anne, Mother of Mary Immaculate, our mother, has entered the fourteenth year of its existence (…) Yes, daughters, very many are the divine mercies with which the year 1879 was filled. The greatest, the most deeply felt and splendid, is that Holy Church, through her Vicar now reigning, Leo XIII, has definitively recognised our family as a religious family, which is as much as to say as a Family of God (…) Following this, the sympathy of the people towards us, who bear the most noble name of Daughters of Saint Anne, is seen ever growing (…) A clear testimony of this sympathy is the many requests received for the foundation of houses in various places.

The foundations established are 19, nine of which have already been opened, and the other ten will soon be opened. Among these new Houses one has been founded in America, in Bolivia, beside the one that was already there. In this one some 80 young girls are educated in religion. Negotiations are under way to found, likewise there in America, three more houses in three different cities, to which 40 Sisters would be called.

This eagerness to have our sisters arises from seeing the prosperous results which the peoples who have them derive from them, both in the Hospitals and in the Schools (…)

The number of those clothed was 57, a number much lower than that of ’78, but the cause was not the scarcity of postulants who asked to put on the habit of the Holy Mother, but that, owing to the critical times we are living in, they have not been able to bring the dowry that is required, little though it is. On the other hand, the Mother House, because of the straitened times, has not been able to open its arms to receive them even without a dowry. And here comes the point to recommend especially to the Superiors: economy, so that, after having maintained and clothed the sisters, they may send the surplus to the Mother House. To this they are bound by love, by vow and by justice. By love: they must know that the fruitfulness of the Institute depends on two heads: the first is that the Lord call many to it even with a very small dowry or none at all. Now the first head has not been lacking this year, for very many were the applications, but the Mother House has lacked the means to receive them without a dowry. Now on whom does it depend that the Mother House have these means? It depends precisely on the economy practised by the Superiors. It is consoling to say that many true daughters of the Holy Mother, eager to see her family spread throughout the whole world, are most attentive to account even for the last penny, as the saying goes, so as to have a surplus to send to the Mother House, knowing that from the well-being of this arises the well-being of the whole Institute. The Mother House is the heart of the Institute; if the Heart is healthy and full of life, the members of the other Houses too are healthy and robust. But this joy the Holy Mother does not receive from all…

Source: Circolare 1880 di M. Rosa e P.G.B. Tornatore · Posiz. Archivio: IIC 80 B.1.63

[Excerpt]

Casting our eye, most beloved daughters, over the whole of this year eighteen hundred and eighty… we have reason to exclaim with the Holy Prophet [?]: O Lord my God, for ever will I sing Your divine mercies. The most signal mercy is that so many of our sisters have been crowned with the crown of eternal happiness (…) they died a death that leaves nothing better to be desired, to assure us that they are in heaven enjoying God in the company of the Holy Mother. Not [?] the good only, but the wicked too have been compelled to pay homage to their charity, which, in imitation of their Divine Master, drove them to sacrifice their bodily life to relieve their neighbour. To their motherly charity shown towards the sick Jesus Christ granted the consolation of leading many back to His loving Divine heart, after long years in which, abandoning Him, they had given themselves to the devil and were on the point of being damned eternally; among these converted sinners there was also a Protestant Heretic, attended by our sisters in the last days of his life. Seeing the truly Christian charity with which they attended him night and day, he recognised that the Roman Church, which knows how to inspire a love of neighbour so disinterested, could only be the one Church of Jesus Christ; whereupon, moved by divine grace… he was converted (…) Ah sisters, with how many souls does the charity of the Institute crown the throne of the Holy Mother, and how it has peopled holy Paradise! But hold firmly, sisters, that all this spiritual fruitfulness which God grants is the reward of the filial love we bear to the Holy Mother, the august and venerable Mother of the Immaculate. She lives in her true daughters, and therefore her true daughters are strong to keep their heart pure from attachment to possessions, to pleasures, to honours, so that, inflamed with the holy love of God, they may be holy themselves and sanctify their neighbour. Therefore the longing to become true and mature Daughters of our Holy Mother must always be alive, honouring her with all those daily devotions which the Institute has established. To this end, and imitating her by the faithful observance of the Holy Rules.

It is their uniform of daughters of Saint Anne, Mother of Mary, that makes them an object of admiration and veneration in the eyes of the people, so that from all sides there are requests for new houses. This year twelve new ones have been opened; but how many more have been the requests which could not be accepted for lack of members! It is true that this year we have clothed one hundred postulants, yet in view of the many houses they are few…

(…) Courage, for it is the time to labour and to suffer, so as one day to have the lot of being all held close to dear Jesus; love much and you will be blessed (Addition to S.A. Giuseppa Troni — Boliv)

Source: Circolare 1881 M. Rosa e P.G.B. Tornatore · Posiz. Archivio: IIC 81 B.1.63

[Excerpt]

This year we have been a little late in sending the circular letter. Providence has so disposed, because it was a matter of opening a new House in America. Now the opening of this is fixed; twelve sisters are needed; therefore those who feel themselves called by God to so holy a mission, let them send us, through their Superiors, their first name and surname. Let those sisters who will go to that Mission know that many souls will, through their work, be led to heaven. The sacrifice these sisters will make in leaving their earthly homeland is for the great glory of God and of the Holy Mother, and assures them the gaining of the heavenly Homeland of holy Paradise. The most noteworthy things that happened last year to the glory of the Institute are: 1st, the departure for America of four sisters for the city of La Paz; 2nd, 138 sisters were clothed, and since the applications of Postulants keep increasing, it was therefore necessary to add a wing to the house, which will hold two hundred beds (…) 16 houses have been opened, and continually there are new requests to open new houses; these requests are a testimony that the Institute draws the sympathy and the esteem of the Bishops and of the Municipalities, of entire populations. In order that the esteem which all have may grow ever more, the observance of the Holy Rules is necessary, especially fidelity to rising, to meditation, to prayer; these are the prayers we make for all of you, dearest Daughters, every day at the feet of the Crucified One. We hope that the Lord will hear us…

Source: Circolare 1882 M. Rosa e P.G.B. Tornatore · Posiz. Archivio: IIC 82 B.1.63

[Excerpt]

Let us never forget, most beloved daughters, that the end for which the heavenly Father has planted the Institute in the garden of His Church is that the August and Venerable Saint Anne, Mother of Mary Immaculate, be honoured in a most singular way by those who are called by her and bear the most noble name of her Daughters. (…)

Now we come to give you news of all the remarkable events that took place in the Institute in the course of the year. 1st. On 23 May the first stone was solemnly laid of the Church that is being built beside the Generalate in Rome (…)

2nd. This year 16 houses were opened and two expeditions were made to America. The first expedition took place on the first of October. Ten sisters left Italy to go to those remote regions, called by Mr Arce to found a new Hospital at Potosí, a city not very far from Sucre; glad and content they bade their last farewell to the Mother House, to go in search of souls and to people Paradise. The second took place on 15 December. Six sisters went to Oruro, another city of Bolivia, to open a new Hospital. The calls that had to be refused for lack of personnel were innumerable. Let us pray, then, to the Holy Mother that the number of postulants may be multiplied, so as to be able to accept the many calls for the opening of new houses.

3rd. The arrival of the Americans filled all the sisters of the Mother House with the greatest consolation. After four months of long waiting they arrived at last on 18 November. When the telegram of their arrival at Genova was received, notwithstanding the poor health the Mother was enjoying, she wanted to go there immediately, but, held back almost by force, she awaited the longed-for day with anxiety (…) We also make known to all the Superiors and Sisters that Sister A. Camilla Valentini, Superior of Sucre, has been elected Provincial and Visitor of Bolivia. And therefore everything she does and disposes, whether for the acceptance of postulants or for the change of sisters, and also for the decision to accept new houses and to stipulate contracts, will be wholly approved and accepted by us. On this matter notice has been given by special letters to the Bishops of Bolivia.

It is also desired that in America the prayers, the chapter and all that our rule prescribes be carried out one day in the Italian language and one day in the Spanish language (…)

We conclude this circular of ours by recommending to those sisters who are in America to observe faithfully the solemn vows and the promises they made at the foot of the Altar before leaving the Mother House…

Source: Circolare 1884 M. Rosa e P.G.B. Tornatore · Posiz. Archivio: IIC 84.3 B.1.63

[Excerpt]

… In the year just past, when God was scourging wretched humanity with the terrible cholera, the Daughters of Saint Anne were the first to succour those poor victims.

And how our nursing sisters displayed their zeal and their charity on behalf of these unfortunate people you will see from a booklet printed expressly for the purpose, and you will learn also how much God is pleased with the mission which our Institute carries out among the sick…

Source: Lettere · Posiz. Archivio: IIC 85-1 B.1.63

[Excerpt]

An Institute is in the flower of observance when the Spirit of Jesus Christ reigns in it. The Spirit of Jesus is manifested principally in the charity that drove Him to die for us. Now, by the mercy of God, the Institute showed itself full of this Spirit this year too. The Lord afflicted the poor city of Palermo with cholera. While the people, terrified by so terrible a pestilence, fled here and there, and the poor stricken by the disease were left abandoned, our sisters, full of the charity of Jesus Christ, went into the midst of the slaughter; and night and day they went round the houses, the streets, bringing every kind of comfort, and they did not leave the victims until they had placed the spirit of the dying in the hands of God and their body in the grave. This spirit of evangelical courage, which joyfully faced the dangers of death to save the life of their brothers, filled with amazement not only the good but also the enemies of our holy religion; and in this way they caused Jesus Christ, the source of such charity, to be glorified both by the good and by the wicked (…) This year eleven houses were opened and thirty sisters sent to America; one hundred and thirty novices were clothed, and thirty passed to a better life…

Source: Circolare 1886 M. Rosa e P.G.B. Tornatore · Posiz. Archivio: IIC 86 B.1.63

[Excerpt]

… Filial love for the Holy Mother is the source of all the graces of heaven. The Holy Mother is the one who leads those who are her true daughters to devotion to Mary Most Holy Immaculate, her daughter; she leads them to the practice of all the virtues proper to their vocation, she leads them to the love of God, in which love holiness consists. Many of these good daughters of the Saint have this year too displayed the spirit of sacrifice; with courage they have undertaken very long journeys, they have gone to America, to Bolivia, to Brazil; they have gone to Africa, not heeding the many dangers met with on such long and hazardous journeys.

This spirit of sacrifice has been shown by those who have been assigned to the care of the sick stricken with contagious diseases: stricken with black smallpox, stricken with the terrible disease of cholera. These sisters have carried themselves with such charity, to such generosity, that they have been a spectacle to heaven and to earth. They faced death with such joy, face to face, as to seem already to see Paradise open before them, the reward of their charity.

These blessings which the Holy Mother pours out upon her Institute must encourage all more and more to long for her with a love ever more tender and ardent, so that as good daughters we have proved it in all their steps [?]; yes, we repeat that this love for their Mother leads to that holiness which God requires of them.

Alongside these virtues, however, we point out some fault, so that, once known, it may be amended by those who recognise it in themselves. This fault concerns in the first place poverty. There are some Superiors who are negligent in sending at the proper time the half-yearly account and, together with the half-yearly account, the surplus. This fault is certainly not slight, because it throws into disorder the ledger in which it is a duty to record them, and it brings harm to the Institute, because, not having the surplus… we cannot carry out those transactions planned for the benefit of the Institute.

Dearest daughters,

Our Circular reaches you later than usual this year: the reason is soon explained. The visitation of Sicily and our illness, brought on by the strain. By the infinite mercy of God our Institute, since the General Chapter, has become much more firmly established, and a great number of houses live in perfect observance, so that in our visits we felt an indescribable consolation, even to the point of being moved.

But one part still harbours the worm of non-observance: little punctuality at meditation, displeasure that the subjects write to us, differences in the food, and so there are [?] partialities, little sincerity with us in setting forth the faults of the sisters.

Superiors, take care to preserve the spirit of the Institute in your communities, so that the poor subjects may not have to fail in their vocation. You will have to render a great account to God for their souls.

Let the subjects, for their part, strive to see in their superior the person of dear Jesus, and not be demanding in wanting the superior to be perfect in everything. Be careful also on this point: not to pass on to one another the faults they see in the Superior.

Dearest daughters, be all charity towards one another. Pray much, and always with that dear little book of our Rules before your eyes and engraved on your heart: and then our poor Institute will be the consolation of God, of the Holy Mother Saint Anne and of the most holy Virgin, in which three hearts we hold you close, praying that this year may be a true triumph of holiness for all;

Pray for our deceased sisters, who numbered 24, of whom 5 died in America. Sisters clothed: 124; houses opened: 13. Imploring from God the most abundant blessings, we remain, for you all,

Rome 1890

Dearest daughters,

It grieves me not a little to have to send you the Circular of 1890 late, and if it were granted me I would not wish to compose it even now; the reason is that it will certainly prove displeasing to you, since I must with bitterness include in it repeated faults, of which we can never obtain the amendment. Dear daughters, my sorrow is most bitter! And what will be the wound that the Holy [?] Mother will receive from it in her maternal heart? Let us then, once and for all, remove these black spots from the work of the Lord and, bound together in a single bond in the love of God, let us seek only his glory, let us abhor self-love and human respect, and let us strive to work for God alone. A superior is removed from office: behold, a crime; the vocation is lost, the head is no longer in its place, she lets herself be possessed by passion, and an infinity of disconnected talk, accusations against the subjects, against the wrong-doing of the superiors; insolent letters are written. Dreadful sin! What? The Saints and Jesus Christ our Divine Master teach us that we must always desire the last places, and thus be sure of walking in the ways of God. The subordinates make a thousand complaints, now wanting to be moved, or, if they are moved too often, they dare to write insolent letters, not thinking that with these they offend the Majesty of God; and I can assure you that this is an outrage not easily blotted out.

Likewise one takes the liberty of wearing finer habits, and in this we deplore great failings against holy poverty.

One also takes the liberty of keeping the belongings of the sisters who leave, a thing said and said again; moreover, when a Superior passes to another house, the one who takes her place always finds faults to uncover in the other.

This practice is to be censured.

We repeat once more with insistence the matter of the railway obedience papers: through your disobedience we have had, and still have, to suffer immensely, with the threat of losing the reduction [?]; and all why? Because you still keep and make use of [? < ti te ?] which are no longer valid, and whoever still has any, let her send them back; and when we write and send obedience papers, we wish you to know well how you must proceed in putting the signature of the head of the party. We also give notice that from the first of July a depository will be opened in Rome at the Generalate for habits, cloth, everything in short that is needed for one of our sisters; in it there will be a sister who will check and will satisfy your requests, sending you [?] the appropriate account. You will remit the indicated sum to her, and so everything will be perfectly uniform.

We desire that, of what we have mentioned above, with lively resolutions and still more with deeds [?], we may see the amendment, and that 1891 may not have to be so painful for us as, we have told you above, the past year has been. Meanwhile pray and offer the usual suffrages by hearing Masses and reciting Rosaries for our poor deceased sisters, who number 16; those clothed are 80, houses opened 7. We wish you a thousand blessings from God, while with all affection I remain:

Dearest daughters,

If what my soul dictates to me to communicate to you were well received on your part, and above all you studied to put the corrections and the prayers into practice, this circular would certainly bring benefit to your houses, setting in order in you whatever non-observance you will find. How I have observed in my visits the indolence, the little account the Superiors make of punctuality in rising and of the treasure of meditation.

It is allowed to be left out; prayers and examens are omitted with great ease; for small matters of their office, the first things to be left out are the obligatory prayers. It is a torment to my soul to see that the Superiors do not consider that, by taking away prayer and exactness of observance, they make themselves guilty before God, giving occasion for the poor subjects to lose the spirit and their vocation. Consider that you will be asked a most strict account of this: and you, dear daughters, who have received so much grace from the Lord, strive to be one thing only with your Superior; act with [?] a right intention, always in the presence of God, with truth in your heart and on your lips. Put away from you that disordered affection for one more than for another; treat one another with respect and equality; be humble with the poor; consider that you are the most wretched of all the creatures who lend their service to the Church and have the good fortune to belong to it. Another thing that gives me great pain is that of seeking [?] a higher office in the Institute, such as wanting to be teachers; oh! if this desire of yours came from a sublime sentiment, such as would be to evangelise and nourish those hearts in the Catechism and so make them strong in our holy Religion; but alas, on this point there is much to deplore! Blessed shall I call the nurses, who surely run the way to heaven! Dearest daughters,

I had promised to send you a second Circular in the time of Lent, but my many occupations and my poor health prevented me.

I take this occasion of the approach of the month of our Holy Mother, Mother of the great Mother of God, Saint Anne. I imagine that all of you will love her with a sincere filial love, and that all of you, vying with one another, will make her ever greater protestations of fidelity, striving to have her honoured and loved by your dear sisters, and not only so, but also by all the peoples among whom you find yourselves. Oh! how dear it is to me when I am on visitation and see the Holy Mother honoured in those little Chapels, or [?] that the superior, wholly intent, promotes devotion to her, and all the graces she desires she seeks to draw from the heart of the mother, close to Jesus and the most holy Immaculate Virgin.

But when instead I find that there are other Saints apart from our mother, poor orphan house, you show yourself so, and by the fact you confirm that you lack what you need.

How many facts I could mention to show you how the Holy Mother, Mother of the great Mother of God, wishes to be invoked by her daughters in their needs, and loved as a mother who carries us to the great most holy Virgin and to the blessed God, holds us close, loves us, so that in these two Hearts of Jesus and Mary you may all be purified and consumed in this most sweet love.

Now allow me to point out to you various points of non-observance, begging you warmly to take account of them and to procure their amendment.

1° Rising in the morning for meditation leaves much to be desired, and as for those who make no account of it, their house soon falls into ruin.

2° The vow of poverty, which so pleases dear Jesus: we and you do not know how to profit from this treasure. A penny saved for love of Jesus, depriving oneself of buying a less useful object: behold a little flower of holy Poverty.

3° Charity with the sisters, and in particular with the Cooks: for these, see to it that they have time to pray, to make their meditation well, and then you will form holy cooks, and it will no longer happen that a change must be made at every moment, because these, not being well cultivated in spirit, always in the office of Martha, grow cold and begin to commit faults.

4° The superior must show herself often in the kitchen and indeed, when she can, try to help, to teach them, to show by example the vow of poverty in practice, the love of holy Obedience; only with this can we acquire the gift of holiness.

5° We also ask you all kindly to send in advance the list of the sisters who are to make their vows for the first time, as well as those who are to make them perpetual; and attach these reports to your accounts. See to it, I repeat, that they are here at least within the first ten days of July, since we are very busy at that time because of the great number of you that the Institute counts.

We wish you a thousand blessings from Heaven, and I embrace you, always held close to my dear Crucified One, remaining in Him:

Rome, May 1892

Your most affectionate Mother S. A. Rosa Gattorno

Dearest daughters,

The great desire we have of being able to see you all according to the Heart of God urges us to send you this second circular, to ask you for clarifications and reports on what we shall tell you below.

1° [?] Not being able, because of our poor health, to be with you as often as before, it is needful to make use of the pen for our peace of mind. An exact report is wanted: 1° on how the holy Rule is observed on the point of rising and meditation, how zealous the sisters are for this, which are the most fervent, and whether the Superior, when she gives them holy Communion, speaks to them of it, exhorts them and teaches them. This is a most necessary point, which binds together all the actions of our day. The resolutions made in Meditation must direct us to act well and to overcome those small faults that we habitually have, so that one day we may see them perfectly blotted out from us. With meditation well made we unite ourselves to God, we ask of him and learn to converse with him, so that everything that is not of God becomes loathsome to us. The actions of the day, done for charity and love of him, make perfect the works entrusted to us. It is recommended to arrange for the holy Exercises and, if possible, that they be made before Saint Anne’s. In those houses where the sisters are few, let them seek to gather in the communities of ours nearest to them.

We also wish to know whether you have sisters who have a vocation to go to America; but first let the superiors give an exact and most scrupulous report on their conduct.

We must then make known to you a displeasure of ours, and it is that of learning that in many houses the sisters do not call one another by the name of Suor Anna and do not respectfully address one another as «Lei»: in this the superiors are the first to fail; this does not please the Holy Mother, and we are much embittered by it. Furthermore we beg you to be [?] more exact in the accounts and to send them more promptly.

We wish you a thousand blessings from God, while in my dear Crucified One I remain:

Rome, 23 April 1893

Your most affectionate Mother S. A. Rosa Gattorno

Dearest daughters.

It [? cfcaplè ?] my soul to have to send you this Circular of mine, which will contain only reproaches, something that pierces the heart of a poor Mother who with so much affection seeks the good and the advantage of your souls. But what sorrow it brings me to have to tell you that, in general, your Houses, O Superiors, are in no way founded on the observance of the holy Rules; still less on exactness in the common acts, which are neglected, as you make little account of the spiritual cultivation of yourselves and of your subjects. What a tremendous account you will have to give to God for so many failings! And yet nothing else is dreamed of, nothing else is held in the heart, but to be Superior. Let me tell you, it is a sin that reigns in the Institute, for which I make sacrifice to God and offer every day as a holocaust all that is humanly given me to do, in reparation for this accursed vice of yours; because each one who has drunk of this water, there is no longer any way that she will take on another Office. She wants reasons for how her removal came about; she thinks of nothing else than of losing even her vocation. You outrage [?] God, to the harm of your soul; consider that only in humility can we be dear to Him. Pride, vanity, vainglory reign in you, and this is what in all my visitations, made in the four months of winter, I have been able to ascertain, and to assure myself of the facts I tell you, of which nothing remains to me but weeping and sorrow.

But no! God will accept my sacrifices and will tear from your heart the barbarous enemy, which is pride, and I am sure that God will give me back daughters full of his love, humble, ready to receive any office, from superior to laundress, from superior to cook; then I shall have nothing else to desire but to repeat the words of the aged Simeon: “Nunc dimittis servum tuum, Domine secundum verbum tuum, in pace.” I return to the point where I said: all my visitations! No, because some of them were a consolation to me, for the observance, the unity between sisters and superior, mutual affection, the superior in the kitchen, the cook together with her, perfect unity, mutual love, exact observance; and these certainly laid upon my wound a balm that served to keep it, poor thing, from turning gangrenous from the very sorrow. And how [?] will the Heart of the Holy Mother not be pierced, if I suffer so much from it? And can these be called Daughters of Saint Anne? Or devourers of souls? “Either Superior, or nothing else, or home!” resounds in all of them! Place yourselves in the presence of God, see a little [?] to making well the meditation on judgement, and consider that a most strict account will be asked of you for the souls entrusted to you.

A terrible thought, which is always before me and [? fa re di esser oltremare ?] me! And that is why I always ask [?] to be taken from this unfortunate post and placed only in the lowest service of the Houses of the Lord. And you cherish so great a desire for it; you never make [? qur ” a ?] meditation, you never place yourselves in the presence of God, you never feel in your heart that an eternity awaits you! You subjects, who so readily answer back to your superiors because they do not have those qualities that you in your imagination believe they ought to have, remember Peter in the Church of the Lord.

Consider that when you answer back or are rude, and do not stand with all due reverence before your Superior, making little account of her admonitions, indeed almost using them for mockery, to whom do you do this? To Jesus himself, because she represents God to you, to set you on the way of perfection, so that you may become his beloved brides.

Superiors, read often what was established in 1888, because alas, of what was established to be put into practice, not one takes any notice. There is the negligence in asking for the vows in time, and then the carelessness, beyond all description, of asking for them by telegram.

Take good care that such things are not repeated.

It is a strict rule that, going out of the house two by two, one may not talk or gesticulate, but must walk in silence and strive to bring the mind to the Passion of Our Lord. Instead the superiors are the first to talk and gesticulate, so much as to cause astonishment even in the lay people who pass by; what is more, they come to me in Rome, ask for a novice to go out and visit the churches, and meanwhile they chatter and give bad example to my novices; from lay people themselves I have to hear that they were scandalised by two sisters who were gesticulating and talking in the street, not once but several times, and in various cities I can say I have noticed it myself.

Recommend to your subjects, when they go out, not to talk, and to consider that while walking they can preach by their bearing, giving edification. Take care that such things never again occur anywhere.

Take care about the vow of poverty! There are Houses in which the Superior makes this vow consist in having the Sisters go about somewhat ragged, deprived of what is necessary, and then money is spent on other useless things; this is not the vow of poverty that the Lord wants from us; read the chapter on the vow of poverty and you will see what Jesus desires us to do.

So too you subjects, who are too fastidious in your clothing, never content, thinking of having more things beyond what is necessary: what thoughts, what attachments are these? It is the instigation of the devil. Come, let us leave these earthly things, let us lift our minds on high and seek to desire those goods that God alone can give. And these are the only ones we shall possess for an eternity, as I so much desire for all of you; and I pray that these words of mine addressed to you may have the good fortune to bear good fruit, all to the glory of God and the honour of our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of Mary Immaculate, in whom I leave you, and in my dear Crucified One I embrace you closely and remain

Rome, 15 June 1894

Your most affectionate Mother S. A. Rosa Gattorno

In the midst of so many sorrows, yes, it is a support that keeps us alive (…)

Allow us to make known to you another affliction of ours. For some years the spirit of self-preservation has entered our poor Institute: the Devil has cleverly managed to enter your sentiments, persuading you that you do this for fear of falling ill and so no longer being fit to work, and therefore a burden to the Institute. Horror! The good sick sisters are our gems. We shall not go on at length to make known to you all the other reports that, alas, are related and written to us.

(…) So for you sacrifice does not exist. Did you become sisters in order to be settled, or rather to correspond to your vocation by having a nest of peace, a sure road that may lead you to the desired Goal? This, however, is acquired only by sacrifice, the self-denial of ourselves, and is reached only by that Religious who thinks solely of increasing her talents, so as to have one day a place nearer to Jesus, in order to enjoy him the more in the Homeland of the Holy Souls.

Strive, dear Daughters, to imitate the virtues of the Holy Mother of the Immaculate Virgin Mary (…) and, held close to the Crucified One, say: You alone for all; in You I wish to live and to be wholly consumed by Your love»…

[…]

[Portuguese translation]

CIRCULAR.

Dearest Daughters,

Having this time to speak only to You, Superiors, allow us to give vent to our soul, oppressed more than ever by the many acts of non-observance committed, which immensely embitter the Heart of God. We find no phrase that can express to you our great sorrow and what we feel!

We do not mean to say that among the great number we do not have Daughters who govern their office so well as to be intent on nothing other than observance and the greater good of their Sisters. These, though few in number, are a consolation to us, and we are comforted by the thought that their prayers and the Blessings that God will pour upon their Houses are what sustain the great edifice of the Lord.

No thought is ever given to the good of the poor Sisters entrusted to them, as is confirmed to us by the negligence in works of piety, and no thought is ever given to procuring a word of comfort for their souls, such as would be: the conferences of some good priest, the Holy Exercises, once a year. Oh! These indeed! How we must stop here to make you know how much your way of acting is to be deplored. If you can, you do everything to avoid them; if compelled by Us and by the confessors themselves, instead of ten days one gets to doing half, and perhaps even three days, and then nothing more is said about it.

What, then, must we say of those poor creatures scattered along the Corridors (of the hospitals); others, alone in the Schools, because the Superior, who ought to watch over them, is now making a little picture to send to her family or to some other person, now flowers to send here or there; and meanwhile the devil makes use of this failing of the Superior to tempt the poor Sisters; and then? One writes in haste: «At once, at once, I found the Sister at fault here and there», and then the thing is made public in a thousand ways, without thinking that You too wear the veil of the Holy Mother and that, by publishing the faults of a Sister, you dishonour yourselves.

A Superior who greatly loves the Institute and venerates her veil, because it was given by God, becomes jealous in all the small actions, observes the evil, sees the danger and keeps silent, does not heed her own interest, but without delay takes the Sister and brings her to Us, with an excuse, without telling a lie; she removes her from danger and no one knows anything. But instead, what is done? Harsh reproofs are made, then one goes to the Confessor, then the matter is communicated to the Sister one loves most; and there is the publicity, ready-made! This point, so delicate, so necessary, must be well observed, because it concerns the honour of the whole Institute.

Another thing still, which the devil comes to whisper in your mind: «The passion for one’s parents.» This year, allow us to tell you, it was a thing that grieved us so much. The Schools close. «[?]», we ask ourselves whether even One alone had said to us: «Mother, let us make the holy Exercises»; before all else I want to be at peace with God. And what then is to be said of that Superior who leaves the Hospital on its own!

Superiors, You who think of nothing else but going to see your relatives, you are the ones who in your religious family do not maintain observance, and worse still, for you make the Sisters all worldly. Superiors, think, think, that on the day of judgement, I repeat to you as I said once before, these will be a great condemnation for you. Instead of giving some little conference, considering that God assists all when one wishes to speak of Him, instead of encouraging the subjects and exhorting them to detachment from relatives, to unite themselves to God, held fast by the bond of his love, what do you do? Think: if you are observant, then that place will be morally uplifted by your conduct, and with this you will gather that good which we religious are obliged to do, it being our holy duty to evangelise the peoples by our conduct.

Therefore it will absolutely no longer be permitted to anyone to go to her family, because we have very painful examples, and then one ends by losing the vocation; and then, when they have grown tired of being with the family, they write, they press, they trouble others in order to re-enter; this is useless, perfectly useless.

You do not even know how to bear a small annoyance from a Sister who, exasperated by your shouting, answers you back. And then one writes to Us: «Transfer her, transfer her.» This happens because you have not done what we said above. And in such a case, why is the Sister not taken gently, why is no effort made to show her affection, caressing her and exhorting her to charity and humility? We, indeed, at times hear: «[?]», sheer nonsense, and we think: «oh! How touchy you are.»

The poor cooks in the hospitals cook all day, and at night they are sent to (keep) vigil. Barbarity! Just try going to the kitchen yourselves, and at night tell us whether you have the legs to keep vigil! Surely there is no cook who satisfies you! Charity, patience; Charity is humble, charity is resigned to the will of God and bears everything, even the small things. Onward, dear Daughters; keep this Circular in your pocket, and read several times in the day what we tell you.

We close, having to add instructions for the Chapter, which will be on 21 October and to which only the Superiors who have No. 12 Sisters in their houses will be summoned. Furthermore, the Superiors of each Province must name three Superiors in whom they have confidence, who will represent the Province in the chapter. Let them write these names on the slip, sending it to Your Provincial. She will carry out the scrutiny, and those Superiors who obtain the greatest number of votes will be admitted to the Chapter. This will serve to appoint the new Provincial and the new Assistants, or to reconfirm them. Do not form parties; see to it that you send your slips to the Provincial as quickly as possible. Pray to the Holy Spirit to enlighten you in the choice and, in the hope that this Circular of ours may bring good effects to your heart, we wish you from God a thousand Blessings, and always in the dear Crucified One.

Piacenza 20 August 1895

Your most sorrowful Mother

S.A. Rosa Gattorno

Source: Portuguese translation by P. Valdo; of the Italian only fragments remain (IIC 95)

[Extract]

If my ignorance could be changed into eloquence, I would wish to show you with worthy expressions how deeply my soul remains moved by your affection and your submission during the General Chapter. The action of the Holy Spirit was in your hearts, in your minds, and bound you in a single bond of love towards me, so unworthy a creature. (…) If nothing has so far been able to halt my step for your good and for the greater Glory of God, I assure you that until the last breath of my life I shall always be the same and shall not fail to come to your aid in any need of yours. (…) Now I shall communicate to you the deliberations taken in the Chapter, which lasted two days (…)

Thus the Chapter ended, to the immense satisfaction of the Most Eminent Protector, who gave an address suited to the occasion, praising the Sisters and exhorting them to persevere in union and in the observance of the Rule (…)

I, for my part, was so moved that, unable to give vent to my soul, I went to give heartfelt thanks to my Crucified One, and with ardent prayers I besought him to preserve such beautiful union in the Institute for all the centuries, until the end of the world. Yes, dear daughters, may there always be in you one heart only, one will only, one love only towards God and the dear Institute, which forms the delight of the Lord and the good pleasure of the Holy Mother, who watches over her Daughters so as to see them one day in a great throng in the Homeland of the Saints.

This year [?] 15 Houses were opened, of which three in Africa and one [?] in Barcelona, the Institute thus extending its branches into Spain as well [?]. The Sisters who passed to a better life were 16, and the novices clothed 110. [?] in the dear Crucified One I am and shall always be Yours.
